questions.question_text:
Virat starts from point B, walks 6 m east, then 4 m south, turns right, walks 4 m, and stops at point Y.

In which direction is point Y with respect to point B?
questions.explanation: After the first two legs Virat faces south; a right turn points west. The 4 m westward leg cancels the 4 m eastward displacement, leaving Y 4 m south of B.
questions.source: Direction and Distance 01_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 1, PDF page 7; topic: direction and distance

questions.question_text:
Ayush walks 2 m east, turns right and walks 3 m, turns left and walks 1 m, then turns north and walks 7 m.

What is the shortest distance from his starting point?
questions.explanation: The east-west displacement is 2 + 1 = 3 m east. The north-south displacement is 7 − 3 = 4 m north. The shortest distance is √(3² + 4²) = 5 m.
questions.source: Direction and Distance 01_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 1, PDF page 10; topic: direction and distance

questions.question_text:
Prachi starts at A, walks 11 km north to B, turns left and walks 12 km to C, turns left and walks 6 km to D, then turns left and walks 12 km to E.

In which direction is point E with respect to point A?
questions.explanation: The west and east legs of 12 km cancel. The net northward displacement is 11 − 6 = 5 km, so E is north of A.
questions.source: Direction and Distance 01_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 1, PDF page 13; topic: direction and distance

questions.question_text:
Shashank starts at R, walks east, then north, turns left and walks to S. The distances of the walks are not specified.

Which direction is S with respect to R?
questions.explanation: Without the lengths of the eastward and northward legs or the final westward leg, S may lie in different directions from R. The direction cannot be determined.
questions.source: Direction and Distance 02_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 2, PDF page 4; topic: direction and distance

questions.question_text:
S is 13 m west of Z; X is 6 m south of Z; R is 5 m west of X; R is 12 m south of T; and P is 6 m north of S.

What is the distance between S and R?
questions.explanation: Taking Z=(0,0), S=(-13,0), X=(0,-6), and R=(-5,-6). The horizontal difference from S to R is 8 m and the vertical difference is 6 m, so the distance is √(8²+6²)=10 m.
questions.source: Direction and Distance 02_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 2, PDF page 7; topic: direction and distance

questions.question_text:
S is 13 m west of Z; X is 6 m south of Z; R is 5 m west of X; R is 12 m south of T; and P is 6 m north of S.

How far and in which direction is X with respect to T?
questions.explanation: From Z=(0,0), X=(0,-6), R=(-5,-6), and since R is 12 m south of T, T=(-5,6). From T to X is 5 m east and 12 m south, giving √(5²+12²)=13 m to the South-East.
questions.source: Direction and Distance 02_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 2, PDF page 7; topic: direction and distance

questions.question_text:
M is 4 m south of P; P is 3 m west of B; B is 4 m north of F; F is 2 m west of Z; Z is 8 m north of H; H is 2 m east of S; and S is 5 m north of J.

In which direction is Z with respect to J?
questions.explanation: Set J=(0,0). Then S=(0,5), H=(2,5), and Z=(2,13). Z is north-east of J.
questions.source: Direction and Distance 02_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 2, PDF page 13; topic: direction and distance

questions.question_text:
M is 4 m south of P; P is 3 m west of B; B is 4 m north of F; F is 2 m west of Z; Z is 8 m north of H; H is 2 m east of S; and S is 5 m north of J.

What is the shortest distance between B and J, and in which direction is J with respect to B?
questions.explanation: Set J=(0,0). S=(0,5), H=(2,5), Z=(2,13), F=(0,13), and B=(0,17). Therefore J is 17 m directly south of B.
questions.source: Direction and Distance 02_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 2, PDF page 13; topic: direction and distance

questions.question_text:
F is 8 m north of K; K is 2 m west of V; V is 4 m north of P; P is 3 m west of C; C is 17 m south of T; T is 3 m east of A; and A is 5 m north of Q.

What is the distance between F and C?
questions.explanation: Set P=(0,0). Then C=(3,0), V=(0,4), K=(-2,4), and F=(-2,12). The separation from F to C is √(5²+12²)=13 m.
questions.source: Direction and Distance 02_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 2, PDF page 16; topic: direction and distance

questions.question_text:
F is 8 m north of K; K is 2 m west of V; V is 4 m north of P; P is 3 m west of C; C is 17 m south of T; T is 3 m east of A; and A is 5 m north of Q.

In which direction is Q with respect to F?
questions.explanation: With P=(0,0), F=(-2,12) and Q=(0,12). Q is 2 m east of F.
questions.source: Direction and Distance 02_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 2, PDF page 16; topic: direction and distance

questions.question_text:
F is 8 m north of K; K is 2 m west of V; V is 4 m north of P; P is 3 m west of C; C is 17 m south of T; T is 3 m east of A; and A is 5 m north of Q.

Which pair is the odd one out by relative direction: F–A, V–T, K–Q, A–V, or P–T?
questions.explanation: Coordinates from P=(0,0) give F=(-2,12), K=(-2,4), V=(0,4), C=(3,0), T=(3,17), A=(0,17), and Q=(0,12). In each listed pair except A–V, the second point is north-east of the first. V is south of A, so A–V is the odd pair.
questions.source: Direction and Distance 02_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 2, PDF page 16; topic: direction and distance

questions.question_text:
A is 3 m west of B; B is 4 m north of C; D is 6 m west of C and 5 m north of E; G is 9 m north of F; and F is 10 m east of E.

In which direction is B with respect to G?
questions.explanation: Set E=(0,0). Then F=(10,0), G=(10,9), D=(-6,5), C=(0,5), B=(-3,9). B and G are on the same horizontal level, with B west of G.
questions.source: Direction and Distance 03_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 3, PDF page 4; topic: direction and distance

questions.question_text:
A is 3 m west of B; B is 4 m north of C; D is 6 m west of C and 5 m north of E; G is 9 m north of F; and F is 10 m east of E.

What is the total distance along the stated route from A to D?
questions.explanation: Set E=(0,0). Then F=(10,0), G=(10,9), D=(0,5), C=(6,5), B=(6,9), and A=(3,9). B and G are on the same horizontal level, with B west of G.
questions.source: Direction and Distance 03_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 3, PDF page 4; topic: direction and distance

questions.question_text:
A is 3 m west of B; B is 4 m north of C; D is 6 m west of C and 5 m north of E; G is 9 m north of F; and F is 10 m east of E.

What is the shortest distance between A and C?
questions.explanation: A is 3 m west and 4 m north of C. By Pythagoras, the shortest distance is √(3²+4²)=5 m.
questions.source: Direction and Distance 03_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 3, PDF page 4; topic: direction and distance

questions.question_text:
A is 5 m north of B; B is 3 m west of C; E is 7 m east of D; D is 5 m north of C; F is 12 m south of E; and G is 8 m west of F.

In which direction is G with respect to C?
questions.explanation: Set C=(0,0). Then D=(0,5), E=(7,5), F=(7,-7), and G=(-1,-7). G is south-west of C.
questions.source: Direction and Distance 03_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 3, PDF page 7; topic: direction and distance

questions.question_text:
Rohan starts at O, walks 4 m east to P, turns left and walks 2 m to Q, turns right and walks 8 m to R, turns right and walks 10 m to S, then walks 9 m west to A.

From A, in which direction and how far must he walk to reach a point 8 m south of O?
questions.explanation: Using O=(0,0), the route ends at A=(3,-8). The target is (0,-8), so A must move 3 m west.
questions.source: Direction and Distance 03_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 3, PDF page 10; topic: direction and distance

questions.question_text:
Sunil walks 20 m east from A, turns left and walks 10 m, turns left and walks 5 m to B, turns right and walks 6 m to C, then walks 8 m to the left of C and stops at D. Separately, a person walks 7 m north from A, turns right and walks 13 m.

In which direction is point D with respect to the second person’s final position?
questions.explanation: Set A=(0,0). Sunil’s route gives D=(7,16). The second person ends at (13,7). From that position to D is 6 m west and 9 m north, so D is north-west.
questions.source: Direction and Distance 03_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 3, PDF page 12; topic: direction and distance

questions.question_text:
Mohan walks from P 40 m north, turns left and walks 60 m, turns right and walks 20 m, then turns left and walks 60 m to Q. Abhay then walks from P 10 m east, turns left and walks 60 m to R.

In which direction is P with respect to Q?
questions.explanation: Set P=(0,0). Mohan’s route puts Q=(-120,60). From Q to P is 120 m east and 60 m south, which is south-east.
questions.source: Direction and Distance 03_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 3, PDF page 14; topic: direction and distance

questions.question_text:
A person starts at B, walks 17 m west to C, turns left and walks 7 m to J, turns right and walks 15 m to X, turns left and walks 14 m to S, turns left and walks 12 m to E, turns left and walks 10 m to A, turns right and walks 18 m to V, turns right and walks 13 m to H, turns right and walks 25 m to Y, then turns left and walks 5 m to R.

What is the approximate shortest distance between A and R?
questions.explanation: Track the net coordinates from the route: relative to A, R is 7 m west and 18 m south. The straight-line distance is √(7²+18²)=√373≈19.3 m, approximately 19 m.
questions.source: Direction and Distance 03_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 3, PDF page 16; topic: direction and distance

questions.question_text:
A person starts at B, walks 17 m west to C, turns left and walks 7 m to J, turns right and walks 15 m to X, turns left and walks 14 m to S, turns left and walks 12 m to E, turns left and walks 10 m to A, turns right and walks 18 m to V, turns right and walks 13 m to H, turns right and walks 25 m to Y, then turns left and walks 5 m to R.

In which direction is J with respect to V?
questions.explanation: Tracking the route gives J=(-17,-7) and V=(-2,-11), relative to the starting point B. From V to J is 15 m west and 4 m north, so J is north-west of V.
questions.source: Direction and Distance 03_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 3, PDF page 16; topic: direction and distance

questions.question_text:
A person starts at B, walks 17 m west to C, turns left and walks 7 m to J, turns right and walks 15 m to X, turns left and walks 14 m to S, turns left and walks 12 m to E, turns left and walks 10 m to A, turns right and walks 18 m to V, turns right and walks 13 m to H, turns right and walks 25 m to Y, then turns left and walks 5 m to R.

If another person at Y walks 10 m east, what is the shortest distance from that person to C?
questions.explanation: On the route, C=(-17,0), Y=(-27,-24). After walking 10 m east the person is at (-17,-24), directly 24 m south of C.
questions.source: Direction and Distance 03_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 3, PDF page 16; topic: direction and distance
